certification.email.media.attachmentAcce: {{host}} accepted a test message carrying a small image attachment.
certification.email.media.attachmentReje: {{host}} refused the message once an attachment was added, most often a size limit or a content filter. The server's own reply is recorded with this result.
certification.email.receive.imapCredenti: {{host}} refused the incoming username and password, so {{folder}} could not be read. Most providers need an app password here rather than the sign-in password.
certification.email.receive.imapUnreacha: Could not reach the incoming server {{host}}, so {{folder}} could not be read. Check the server name, the port and the SSL setting.
certification.email.receive.mailboxReada: Signed in to {{host}}, opened {{folder}} read-only and searched it. No message was fetched and nothing was marked as read.
certification.email.receive.mailboxRefus: {{folder}} opened on {{host}}, but the server refused to search it, which is the next step in collecting replies. Check this folder with your mail provider.
certification.email.receive.polledFolder: {{host}} would not open the folder {{folder}}. Check the spelling and that the folder exists in this mailbox — a folder that is not there means replies are never picked up.
certification.email.send.acceptedForDeli: {{host}} accepted the test message for delivery.
certification.email.send.noFromAddressTo: No from address is stored, so there is nothing to send as. Mail without a sender is refused or treated as spam by every receiving server. Edit the channel and set the from address.
certification.email.send.rejectedByTheSe: {{host}} refused the test message. The server's own reply is recorded with this result.
certification.email.send.someRecipientsR: The message was handed over, but {{host}} refused one or more recipients. The refused addresses are recorded with this result.
certification.email.send.storedValuesDoN: The stored settings do not make a valid message — usually a from address with a line break or a stray character in it. Re-enter the from address and run this again.
certification.email.skipped.aPasswordHas: A mailbox password has no expiry and cannot be renewed automatically. When a provider revokes one, somebody has to create a new app password, so there was nothing to test.
certification.email.skipped.noProviderSe: A mailbox holds nothing on Blink Engage's behalf — no session and no registration — so there is nothing to disconnect and nothing to reconnect.
certification.email.skipped.noWebhookInb: Email has nowhere for a provider to deliver to. Replies are collected by checking the {{folder}} folder on a schedule, so there was nothing to test here.
certification.email.skipped.probeAnswere: The mail server was contacted but gave nothing back to judge, so this was left unanswered rather than counted as a pass.
certification.email.skipped.providerMeth: Email has no read receipts and no typing indicator to send, so there was nothing to run here.
certification.email.skipped.sendOnlyMail: This mailbox has no incoming settings, so there is nothing to read. Nothing was tested here.
certification.email.skipped.targetIsNotA: The test target is not an email address, so nothing was sent. Enter an address to send the test message to.
certification.email.skipped.wouldHaveToR: Testing a received attachment would mean opening real mail in your mailbox and marking it as read. This test does not do that, so it was not run.
certification.notImplemented: This channel does not run this check yet, so there is no result to report.
certification.raised: This check stopped with an unexpected error and did not finish. Run the checks again; if it keeps happening, send this report to support.
certification.skipped.credentialsIncompl: Part of this channel's stored credentials is missing, so the check could not run. Edit the channel, enter the credentials again, then run the checks.
certification.skipped.needsInboundMedia: This check needs a file somebody sent in, and a test run cannot make one arrive. Send an image to this channel from another account, then run the checks again.
certification.skipped.needsInboundMessag: Only a real incoming message can start this check, and a test run cannot make one arrive. Message this channel from another account, then run the checks again.
Marking a message as read needs an incoming message to mark, and there is none. Message this channel from another account, then run the checks again.
certification.skipped.noAppCredentials: Renewing the token needs the provider app's own credentials, which this check is not given, so renewal was not tested.
certification.skipped.noProviderDisconne: This provider has no disconnect step of its own to run. To disconnect the channel, remove it from your channel list.
certification.skipped.noTarget: No test recipient was given, so nothing was sent. Enter a number or account that can receive a test message, then run the checks again.
certification.skipped.notMeasured: Nothing was measured for this check, so there is no result. Run the checks again.
certification.skipped.providerThrottled: The provider is limiting how often we may call it right now, so this was not measured. Run the checks again in a few minutes.
certification.skipped.providerUnreachabl: The provider could not be reached, so this was not measured. It does not mean the channel is broken — run the checks again once the provider is responding.
certification.skipped.subscriptionNodeUn: Incoming messages for this channel are registered on the business account above it, which this check cannot see. Nothing is wrong — this part simply cannot be measured from here.
certification.skipped.targetNotReachable: The provider would not deliver to the test recipient, so nothing about this channel was measured. Usually they last wrote to you more than 24 hours ago, or are not on the provider app's list of test recipients — try someone who has messaged you recently.
certification.skipped.timedOut: Time ran out before the provider answered, so nothing was measured. Run the checks again — a slow provider is the usual cause.
certification.skipped.tokenExchangeUnimp: Renewing credentials is not built for this channel yet, so there was nothing to test.
certification.skipped.wouldChangeTheChan: This check changes how the channel is connected, so it only runs when you ask for it. Turn on the checks that change the channel and run them again.
certification.sms.authenticated: The carrier accepted the stored credentials.
certification.sms.messageAccepted: A test message to {{target}} was accepted by the carrier and billed as one segment. Acceptance is what was measured; arrival on the handset was not observed.
certification.sms.sendRejected: The carrier refused the test message to {{target}}. The provider code recorded with this result says why — commonly an unverified recipient on a trial account, or a sender number that cannot carry SMS.
certification.sms.skipped.carrierDidNotA: The carrier said nothing about {{diagnostic}}, so it was not measured. That is an unanswered question rather than a failure — usually the account check stopped before this one could run.
certification.sms.skipped.carrierSendNot: No test message was sent. This installation has no way to send one through {{gateway}} that it could tell apart from your ordinary traffic, so sending stays unproven rather than assumed.
certification.sms.skipped.gatewayUnknown: This channel is stored against {{gateway}}, which this installation cannot load, so nothing was run. The same channel on an installation that ships {{gateway}} would certify normally.
certification.sms.skipped.inboundNeedsAR: Receiving was not tested. It needs someone to actually text this number, which a test run must not arrange and cannot fake: the carrier's own log would only prove that the carrier received something, never that we did.
certification.sms.skipped.mediaNeedsARea: Picture download was not tested. It needs a real incoming MMS, and the only ones this account holds belong to your customers — reading one to score ourselves is not a trade we will make.
certification.sms.skipped.noRefreshableC: There is nothing to refresh. An SMS auth token is a fixed secret you type in, not a credential that expires and renews itself, so this does not apply to this channel.
certification.sms.skipped.nothingToDisco: There is nothing to disconnect and reconnect. SMS holds no session that can be dropped, and the one link that could be cut — the number's incoming-message address — could not be put back from here, which would leave a working channel unable to receive.
certification.sms.skipped.sendUnconfirme: The test message to {{target}} could not be confirmed. No message id came back, so nothing can be pointed at — but it may still have been sent and billed. Check the carrier's message log before running this again.
certification.sms.webhookPointsHere: The number's incoming-message address points at this installation.
certification.telegram.authenticatedAs: Telegram accepted the token and identified the bot as {{botName}}.
certification.telegram.botTokenMissing: Not run: no bot token is stored for this channel, so nothing could be attempted.
certification.telegram.botTokensDoNotExp: Not run: Telegram bot tokens do not expire, so there is nothing to renew. A token stops working only when you revoke it in BotFather.
certification.telegram.chatActionAccepte: Telegram accepted a typing indicator for the chat you named. That is as far as this can be checked — Telegram reports nothing about whether it appeared.
certification.telegram.fileDownloaded: A file was downloaded from Telegram in full, by the same route incoming attachments take.
certification.telegram.inboundCannotBePr: Not run: receiving can only be proven by a real person messaging the bot, and nothing here may cause that. Message the bot yourself and check it appears in your inbox.
certification.telegram.messageSent: A test message was sent to the chat you named, and Telegram confirmed it with a message id.
certification.telegram.messageUnconfirme: Telegram accepted the test message but returned no id for it, so there is no proof it reached the chat. Open the chat to confirm.
certification.telegram.noFileToDownload: Not run: there was no file to download in the chat you named. Use a chat that has a photo, or a one-to-one chat with someone who has a profile picture.
certification.telegram.noTargetChat: Not run: no test chat was given. Enter the id of a Telegram chat this bot can write to, then run it again.
certification.telegram.notMeasured: Not run: Telegram gave no answer this check could be judged on.
certification.telegram.photoSent: A test image was uploaded and delivered to the chat you named, and Telegram confirmed it holds the file.
certification.telegram.photoUnconfirmed: Telegram accepted the test image but did not confirm it holds the file, so the upload is unproven. Open the chat to confirm.
certification.telegram.providerUnreachab: Not run: Telegram did not answer. Run this again once Telegram is responding.
certification.telegram.rejectedByProvide: Telegram refused this request. The channel cannot do this as it is set up now — see the details recorded with this result.
certification.telegram.throttled: Not run: Telegram is limiting how often this bot may call it. Run this again in a few minutes.
certification.telegram.tokenNotAccepted: Telegram did not accept this bot token. Issue a new one from @BotFather and update the channel.
certification.telegram.unexpectedFailure: This check failed for a reason we did not expect. The error is recorded with this result; send it to support.
certification.telegram.webhookBacklog: Telegram is holding {{pending}} messages for this bot that have not been handed over. Run Restore message delivery, then watch the number fall.
certification.telegram.webhookDeliveryFa: Telegram could not deliver to us at {{at}}: {{detail}}. Messages sent around then did not arrive.
certification.telegram.webhookNotRegiste: Telegram has nowhere to deliver this bot's messages, so this channel receives nothing. Run Restore message delivery.
certification.telegram.webhookRegistered: Telegram is delivering this bot's messages to {{host}}, with nothing queued and no recent failures.
Telegram is delivering this bot's messages to {{host}}, which is not an address of ours. Check whether another tool is connected to the same bot; otherwise run Restore message delivery.
certification.telegram.webhookSecretNotR: Not run: taking delivery down and putting it back would leave this bot silently unable to verify incoming messages. Use Restore message delivery instead — it does this safely.
check.business_verification_required: The provider needs your business verified first.
check.provider_unreachable: We could not reach the provider. Try again shortly.
check.rate_limited: The provider is asking us to slow down. Try again shortly.
check.unsupported_api_version: This provider no longer supports the version we are using.
check.webhook_not_registered: Incoming messages are not set up yet.
connect.email.check.inbound: We check whether this mailbox is also set up to be read, so replies from your customers arrive here.
connect.email.check.inbound.title: Incoming replies
connect.email.check.sendOnly: This mailbox can send, but nothing will be read from it. Replies your customers write stay in the mailbox and never reach a conversation here.
connect.email.check.smtp: We open a connection to your outgoing server and sign in with the details you entered. No mail is sent.
connect.email.check.smtp.title: Outgoing mail
connect.email.check.tlsPortMismatch: The TLS setting does not match port {{port}}. Port 465 needs TLS on; port 587 needs it off, because that connection starts in plain text and is upgraded.
connect.email.description: Connect a mailbox you already own. Blink Engage sends through your outgoing mail server, and — if you add the incoming settings — collects your customers' replies from the mailbox as conversations.
connect.email.diagnostic.inboundIncomple: The incoming server is set but the username or password is missing, so the {{folder}} folder is never read and replies sit in the mailbox unseen. Add the missing incoming details.
connect.email.diagnostic.noWebhookAndNoI: Nothing is read from this mailbox. It has no incoming settings, so it sends only, and every reply a customer writes stays in the mailbox. Add the incoming settings if replies should arrive here.
connect.email.diagnostic.noWebhookInboun: Email has no callback to register. Replies are collected by checking the {{folder}} folder on a schedule, and that check has not been observed yet — a wrong password, or a folder your mail rules move mail out of, would look exactly like this.
connect.email.diagnostic.serverSpeaksEsm: {{host}} answered as an ESMTP server, so sign-in and encryption are available on port {{port}}.
connect.email.diagnostic.serverWithoutEs: {{host}} answered as a plain SMTP server on port {{port}}: it offers no sign-in and no encryption, so mail leaves this system unencrypted and no new password will ever be accepted. Move to a server or port that supports encryption if this mail is sensitive.
connect.email.diagnostic.smtpCredentials: {{host}} accepted the stored username and password on port {{port}}. This mailbox can send.
{{host}} refused the stored username and password, so nothing is being sent. A new app password has to be created for this mailbox and saved here. Details: {{detail}}
connect.email.diagnostic.smtpHostMissing: No outgoing server is saved for this channel, so nothing can be sent. Edit the channel and enter the outgoing server and port.
connect.email.diagnostic.smtpRelayAccept: No password is stored for this mailbox, and {{host}} accepts mail from this system without one. No sign-in was tested — the relay itself decides who may send through it.
connect.email.diagnostic.smtpUnreachable: Could not reach {{host}} on port {{port}}, so this mailbox is not sending. Check the server name, the port, and whether a firewall or the mail host is blocking the connection. Details: {{detail}}
connect.email.feature.inboundRequiresIma: Replies arrive only when the incoming (IMAP) settings are filled in. Without them this channel sends and nothing comes back.
connect.email.feature.mediaTravelsInside: Files travel inside the message itself, so the size limit is whatever the receiving mail server accepts — and a message over that limit is refused whole rather than trimmed.
connect.email.feature.threadingByHeaders: Each reply is linked to the message it answers, but the link is invisible to the reader: mail apps group the messages into one thread instead of showing a quoted reply.
connect.email.fix.addImapSettings: Go back a step and fill in the incoming server, username and password to have replies collected. Leave them blank to keep this mailbox for sending only.
connect.email.fix.smtpCredentials: {{host}} refused the username and password. Check both, and note that Gmail, Microsoft 365 and most providers require an app password created for this mailbox rather than your sign-in password. Details: {{detail}}
connect.email.fix.smtpUnreachable: We could not reach {{host}} on port {{port}}. Check the server name and the port, and whether a firewall is blocking outgoing mail from this system. Details: {{detail}}
connect.email.fix.tlsPortPairing: Use port 465 with TLS on, or port 587 with TLS off. Port {{port}} with the current setting is a pairing almost no mail server accepts.
connect.email.fromAddressHelp: The address your mail is sent from, and the one your customers reply to. Use a mailbox this server is allowed to send as, or messages will be refused or treated as spam.
connect.email.imapFolderHelp: The folder checked for new mail, INBOX unless you change it. If your own mail rules move incoming mail to another folder, name that folder here or nothing will be picked up.
connect.email.imapHostHelpSendOnlyWithou: The incoming mail server, such as imap.example.com. Leave it blank and this channel only sends — replies stay in your mailbox and nobody here sees them.
connect.email.imapPasswordHelpSendOnlyWi: As with sending, most providers need an app password here. Without it, replies cannot be collected and this channel only sends.
connect.email.imapPortHelp: Usually 993 with SSL, or 143 without it.
connect.email.imapUseSslHelp: Keep this on for port 993, the standard encrypted port. Turn it off only for a server that expects a plain connection on port 143.
connect.email.imapUsernameHelpSendOnlyWi: Usually the full mailbox address. Without it, replies cannot be collected and this channel only sends.
connect.email.name: Email
connect.email.smtpHostHelp: The outgoing mail server your provider gave you, such as smtp.example.com. Everything sent from this channel goes through it.
connect.email.smtpPasswordHelp: Gmail, Microsoft 365 and most providers need an app password created for this mailbox, not the password you sign in with. Leave it blank only if the server asks for no password.
connect.email.smtpPortHelp: Usually 587, or 465 if your provider encrypts the connection from the first byte. Set it to match the TLS setting below.
connect.email.smtpUseTlsHelpPairWithPort: Turn this on for port 465, which is encrypted from the start. Leave it off for port 587, which begins in plain text and is upgraded to encryption. Mismatching the two is the most common reason a correct mailbox cannot send.
connect.email.smtpUsernameHelp: Usually the full mailbox address. Leave it blank only for an internal relay that accepts mail from this server without a password.
connect.instagram.description: Answer the direct messages sent to your Instagram professional account. The account must be a Business or Creator account linked to a Facebook Page.
connect.instagram.features.mediaNoDocume: Images, video and audio only. Instagram does not accept documents such as PDF files, and a reply with one attached is rejected.
connect.instagram.name: Instagram
connect.instagram.resources.empty: No Instagram accounts found. Only a professional account — Business or Creator — linked to a Facebook Page can be connected. A personal account cannot.
connect.instagram.resources.title: Choose the Instagram accounts to connect
connect.messenger.description: Answer the messages people send to your Facebook Pages. Connect every Page you manage — each one becomes its own channel.
connect.messenger.name: Facebook Messenger
connect.messenger.resources.empty: No Facebook Pages found. You need to be an admin of at least one Page, and the Page has to be included when you approve access for Meta.
connect.messenger.resources.title: Choose the Pages to connect
connect.meta.accessToken.help: Use a permanent token, not the temporary one Meta shows by default — that one stops working within 24 hours. For WhatsApp use a System User token; for a Page or an Instagram account use that Page's access token.
connect.meta.accessToken.label: Access token
connect.meta.appSecret.help: From your Meta app → Settings → Basic → App Secret. Meta signs every incoming message with it, so it has to match exactly: a wrong value saves without complaint and then drops every message silently.
connect.meta.appSecret.label: App Secret
connect.meta.check.permissions: Your access token works, and Meta granted every permission this channel needs.
connect.meta.check.permissions.title: Permissions
connect.meta.check.resource: The number, Page or Instagram account you chose can send and receive messages.
connect.meta.check.resource.title: Selected account
connect.meta.features.mediaSeparateMessa: Messenger cannot carry text and an attachment in one message, so a reply containing both arrives as two messages.
connect.meta.fix.instagramInbox: Instagram passes messages to other apps only while the account owner allows it, and that switch exists only in the phone app. In Instagram, open Settings → Messages and story replies → Connected tools and turn on "Allow access to messages". Without it the channel connects and no messages arrive.
connect.meta.fix.noMessagingRights: You can manage this Page but not send messages from it. Ask a Page admin to give you the Messaging task in Meta Business settings → Pages → People, then try again here.
connect.meta.fix.numberNotVerified: Meta has not finished verifying this number. Open WhatsApp Manager, select the number, complete the verification code step, then try again here.
connect.meta.instagram_id.help: The ID of the Instagram professional account, not its username. In Meta Business settings, open Accounts → Instagram accounts and copy the ID under the account. The account must be linked to a Facebook Page.
connect.meta.instagram_id.label: Instagram account ID
connect.meta.page_id.help: In Meta Business settings, open Accounts → Pages, select your Page and copy the Page ID shown under its name.
connect.meta.page_id.label: Page ID
connect.meta.phone_number_id.help: In Meta for Developers, open your app → WhatsApp → API Setup and copy the Phone number ID. It is not the phone number shown beside it.
connect.meta.phone_number_id.label: Phone number ID
connect.meta.repair.reregisterWebhook.de: Asks Meta to send this channel's messages to Blink Engage again. Use it when messages stopped arriving while the account and the access token are still good.
connect.sms.check.account.title: Checking your carrier account
connect.sms.check.accountInactive: The credentials work, but the carrier account is {{status}} rather than active. Nothing will send until the account is back in good standing.
connect.sms.check.accountTrial: This is a trial account. It can only message numbers that have been verified with the carrier, so the channel works for whoever tested it and for nobody else.
connect.sms.check.credentialMissing: The carrier you chose needs {{field}}. Fill that field in and run the check again.
connect.sms.check.credentialsRejected: The carrier refused these credentials. Check the Account SID and Auth Token against your carrier console and paste them in again — a stray space, or a token that has been rotated since, is the usual cause.
connect.sms.check.gatewayUnknown: The selected carrier ({{gateway}}) is not one this installation can send through. Choose a carrier from the list.
connect.sms.check.gatewayUnreachable: We could not reach the carrier to check these credentials: {{detail}}. This is usually a passing outage or a firewall between us and the carrier. Try again in a few minutes.
connect.sms.check.number.title: Checking your sender number
connect.sms.check.numberNoSms: {{number}} is on the account but is not set up to carry SMS — it is a voice-only number, and messages sent from it will be refused.
connect.sms.check.numberNotOnAccount: {{number}} is not on this carrier account, so nothing will send from it. Check it for a typo, or use a number the account actually owns.
connect.sms.check.numberUnverified: The credentials are correct, but the carrier would not return the account's number list, so the sender number is unchecked: {{detail}}. Sending may well work. Try again, or confirm in the carrier console that the number is on this account and can carry SMS.
connect.sms.check.numberVerified: {{number}} is on this account and can send SMS.
connect.sms.check.webhookAutomatic: Incoming messages need no setup from you. As soon as you save, we point your number at this channel.
connect.sms.check.webhookManualSetup: This carrier cannot be pointed at us automatically. Sending will work as soon as you save; incoming messages wait on one setting you copy into the carrier's console.
connect.sms.description: Text messages to and from a phone number on your own carrier account. You send text; customers can send text and pictures.
connect.sms.diagnostic.accountInactive: The credentials are accepted, but the carrier account is {{status}} rather than active. Nothing will send while it stays that way — clear it in the carrier console.
connect.sms.diagnostic.accountTrial: This is a trial carrier account. It reaches only numbers that have been verified with the carrier, so anyone else who texts in gets no reply. Upgrade the account before putting customers on this channel.
connect.sms.diagnostic.apiVersionMismatc: Your number is set to an older carrier API version than {{expected}}. Incoming messages arrive in a shape we cannot read and are lost. In the carrier console, set the number's API version to {{expected}}.
connect.sms.diagnostic.credentialsReject: The carrier is refusing the stored credentials. Sending and receiving are both down until the Account SID and Auth Token are re-entered from the carrier console.
connect.sms.diagnostic.gatewayUnknown: This channel is stored against {{gateway}}, which this installation cannot load, so nothing could be checked. Reconnect the channel using a carrier from the current list.
connect.sms.diagnostic.gatewayUnreachabl: The carrier could not be reached, so nothing on this channel was measured: {{detail}}. Check that this installation can make outbound requests to the carrier, then run the check again.
connect.sms.diagnostic.numberNotOnAccoun: The carrier account no longer holds {{number}}. No incoming message can reach this channel, and no repair here can change that. Put the number back on the account, or reconnect this channel with a number the account owns.
connect.sms.diagnostic.numberUnreadable: The credentials work, but the carrier would not return this number's settings, so we cannot say where incoming messages are being delivered: {{detail}}. Run the check again.
connect.sms.diagnostic.providerError: The carrier answered with a problem of its own rather than anything about this channel, so this could not be measured. The stored credentials were not called into question. Try again in a few minutes.
connect.sms.diagnostic.rateLimited: The carrier is throttling this account right now. Requests are being refused until the limit resets; the credentials and the number are not at fault.
connect.sms.diagnostic.webhookElsewhere: Your number is delivering incoming messages somewhere other than this installation, so anything customers text goes there instead. Run Reconnect incoming messages to point it back.
connect.sms.diagnostic.webhookMethod: The address is ours, but the carrier is set to deliver with {{method}} instead of POST, and messages arrive empty. Run Reconnect incoming messages to correct it.
connect.sms.diagnostic.webhookMissing: Your number has no incoming-message address set at the carrier, so nothing customers text you arrives. Run Reconnect incoming messages to set it.
connect.sms.diagnostic.webhookUnverifiab: Your number has an incoming-message address set, but this installation has no public address configured, so we cannot tell whether that address is ours. Set the public address for this installation and check again.
connect.sms.error.callbackUrlMissing: This channel has no inbound address yet, so there is nothing to point the carrier at. Reload the channel and run the repair again.
connect.sms.error.credentialMissing: A credential this carrier needs is missing, so the channel was not created. Go back to the form and fill in every field the carrier you chose requires.
connect.sms.error.gatewayUnknown: This channel is stored against a carrier this installation cannot load, so incoming messages could not be set up. Reconnect the channel and choose a carrier from the current list.
connect.sms.error.numberNotOnAccount: The sender number is no longer on the carrier account, so incoming messages could not be set up. Put the number back on the account, or reconnect this channel with a number it owns.
connect.sms.error.webhookRegistrationFai: We could not set the incoming-message address at your carrier. Sending is unaffected. Run the repair again, or set the number's incoming-message URL by hand in the carrier console.
connect.sms.feature.mediaInboundOnly: Incoming only. Pictures a customer texts you arrive and are saved; you cannot send one back.
connect.sms.feature.textOnly: Text only. A file or image attached to an outgoing message will not be sent.
connect.sms.fix.setInboundWebhook: After you save, copy the inbound address shown on the channel's page into your carrier console as the number's incoming-message URL, and set the method to POST.
connect.sms.gatewayHelp: The company that delivers your text messages. Choose it first: the fields below belong to whichever one you pick, and only those are checked.
connect.sms.name: SMS
connect.sms.repair.reregisterWebhook.des: Points your number back at this channel. Use it when messages stop arriving while sending still works — anyone with access to the carrier console can change that setting, and the only symptom is silence. Running it more than once changes nothing.
connect.sms.twilio.accountSidHelp: Starts with AC. Find it on the home page of the Twilio Console, under Account Info.
connect.sms.twilio.authTokenHelp: Next to the Account SID in the Twilio Console. This one value both sends your messages and proves that incoming ones really came from Twilio, so if you rotate it there, paste the new one here as well — otherwise sending and receiving stop together.
connect.sms.twilio.fix.activateAccount: Open the Twilio Console and clear whatever is holding the account — usually an unpaid balance or a suspension notice — then run this check again.
connect.sms.twilio.fix.buyNumber: In the Twilio Console, open Phone Numbers → Manage → Active numbers and copy a number listed there. If the account has none, buy one under Buy a number.
connect.sms.twilio.fix.leaveTrial: Upgrade the account in the Twilio Console to lift the verified-numbers restriction. Until you do, add each recipient under Phone Numbers → Verified Caller IDs.
connect.sms.twilio.fix.smsCapability: In the Twilio Console, open Phone Numbers → Manage → Active numbers and choose one whose capabilities include SMS. Not every number sold in every country can carry text.
connect.sms.twilio.fromNumberHelp: The Twilio number this channel sends from, in full international format with the + and country code. It has to be on the account above and able to carry SMS.
connect.telegram.botToken.help: The token BotFather gave you when you created the bot. In Telegram, message @BotFather and send /newbot, then paste the token it replies with.
connect.telegram.botToken.label: Bot token
connect.telegram.check.delivery: Checking whether Telegram has been able to deliver this bot's messages to us.
connect.telegram.check.delivery.title: Message delivery
connect.telegram.check.identity: Confirming which bot this token belongs to.
connect.telegram.check.token: Checking that Telegram accepts this token, and which bot it belongs to.
connect.telegram.check.token.title: Bot token
connect.telegram.description: Connect a Telegram bot so customers can message you there and your team replies from the same inbox.
connect.telegram.docs.botFather: How to create a bot with BotFather
connect.telegram.error.botTokenMissing: No bot token. Paste the token BotFather gave you, then try again.
connect.telegram.error.botTokenRejected: Telegram did not accept this bot token. Check that you copied all of it, or message @BotFather and send /token to get a new one.
connect.telegram.error.callbackUrlMissin: There is no connected channel to deliver to yet. Finish connecting this bot — delivery is set up for you as part of that — and this resolves itself.
connect.telegram.error.webhookRegistrati: Telegram did not accept the delivery address for this bot, so messages your customers send will not reach you. Run Restore message delivery to try again.
connect.telegram.feature.edit.note: Only message text can be edited. Captions on photos and files you have already sent cannot be changed.
connect.telegram.feature.media.note: Photos and files work in both directions. Video, voice notes and stickers your customers send arrive as their caption text only, without the file.
connect.telegram.feature.typing.note: The typing indicator shows for a few seconds and clears on its own — Telegram offers no way to stop it sooner.
connect.telegram.fix.issueToken: Open Telegram and message @BotFather. Send /newbot to create a bot, or /token to get a fresh token for a bot you already have, then paste it here.
connect.telegram.name: Telegram
connect.telegram.repair.reregisterWebhoo: Tells Telegram again where to deliver this bot's messages. Use it when messages stop arriving, or when another tool has been connected to the same bot.
connect.template.fullMetaSuite.descripti: Connect WhatsApp, Messenger and Instagram in one pass. You approve once, and each one becomes its own channel.
connect.template.fullMetaSuite.title: All Meta channels
connect.template.instagramMessenger.desc: Connect your Instagram accounts and your Facebook Pages together. One approval covers both.
connect.template.whatsappOnly.descriptio: Connect one WhatsApp Business number on its own. You approve the WhatsApp permissions and nothing about Pages or Instagram.
connect.template.whatsappOnly.title: WhatsApp only
connect.web_chat.certify.inboundComesFro: An incoming message arrives when a visitor types in the chat widget, which this check cannot do. Open the widget on your site and send a message to see it work.
connect.web_chat.certify.needsTheProvide: Sending only happens inside a live visitor session, which this check cannot open. Open the chat widget on your site and reply from the console to see it work.
connect.web_chat.certify.noCredentialToA: Web Chat has no credentials to sign in with, so there was nothing to test.
connect.web_chat.certify.noProviderSideR: Web Chat is not registered with any outside service, so there is nothing to disconnect from or reconnect to.
connect.web_chat.certify.noWebhookToDeli: Web Chat has no webhook. Messages arrive over the visitor's own live connection, so there is no delivery to test.
connect.web_chat.certify.notExercisableH: This check cannot be run against Web Chat, so it was skipped.
connect.web_chat.certify.nothingToRefres: Nothing here expires. A visitor's session times out in their browser, but the channel itself holds no credentials to renew.
connect.web_chat.check.noExternalDepende: Web Chat depends on no outside service, so there is nothing here to verify. The file storage it uses is ours, and the automatic health check reports on it once the channel is connected.
connect.web_chat.description: A chat widget for your own website. There is no account to sign in to and nothing to paste — visitors message you straight from their browser.
connect.web_chat.diagnose.noCredentialTo: Web Chat stores no credentials, so there is nothing to check here. That is how the channel works, not a check still waiting to run.
connect.web_chat.diagnose.noProviderScop: There is no outside service behind Web Chat, so no permissions were ever granted and none can be checked.
connect.web_chat.diagnose.noWebhookToReg: Messages arrive over the visitor's own live connection to your site, not through a webhook, so there is no registration to check.
connect.web_chat.feature.media.widgetSup: Agents can send files to visitors, but your chat widget has to be built to display them — the published widget protocol does not describe attachments yet.
connect.web_chat.name: Web Chat
connect.whatsapp.description: Answer customers who write to your WhatsApp Business number. Text, images, video, audio and documents travel both ways.
connect.whatsapp.features.readReceipts: Read receipts go one way. Your customers' messages are marked as read on their phones; WhatsApp does not tell you whether they have read your replies.
connect.whatsapp.name: WhatsApp
connect.whatsapp.resources.empty: No WhatsApp numbers found. Add a number to your WhatsApp Business account in Meta Business settings, and check that you approved the business account the number belongs to.
connect.whatsapp.resources.title: Choose a WhatsApp number
diagnostics.lastFailure: Last recorded failure: {{event}}. Open this channel's connection log to see the full entry.
diagnostics.neverChecked: This channel has not been checked yet, so its state is unknown. Use Test connection to check it now, or wait for the next automatic check.
diagnostics.telegram.apiUnversioned: Telegram's bot API carries no version number, so there is no version to report here and nothing to keep up to date.
diagnostics.telegram.authenticatedAs: Telegram accepts this token and it belongs to @{{username}} (id {{botId}}). Check this is the bot your customers message, not a test one.
diagnostics.telegram.botTokenMissing: No bot token is stored for this channel, so nothing about it can work. Reconnect the channel and paste the token from BotFather.
diagnostics.telegram.botTokenRejected: Telegram rejected this bot token — it was changed or revoked. Message @BotFather, send /token to issue a new one, then update the channel.
diagnostics.telegram.deliveryFailure: Telegram could not deliver to us the last time it tried: {{detail}}. If messages are still not arriving, run Restore message delivery.
diagnostics.telegram.pendingUpdates: Telegram is holding a backlog of this bot's messages that it has not been able to hand over. Run Restore message delivery, then watch the number fall.
diagnostics.telegram.pendingUpdatesUndel: Telegram is queueing this bot's messages with nowhere to deliver them, and drops them after a few days. Run Restore message delivery to start receiving them.
diagnostics.telegram.providerUnreachable: Telegram did not answer, so this could not be checked. Nothing is known to be wrong with the channel — check again in a few minutes.
diagnostics.telegram.throttled: Telegram is limiting how often this bot may call it and asked us to wait. This clears on its own; check again shortly.
diagnostics.telegram.webhookNotRegistere: Telegram has nowhere to deliver this bot's messages, so nothing your customers send is reaching you. Run Restore message delivery.
diagnostics.telegram.webhookRegisteredEl: Telegram is delivering this bot's messages to {{host}}, not to us. If another tool is connected to the same bot, disconnect it there; otherwise run Restore message delivery.
diagnostics.unhealthy.configuration: The provider rejected this channel's credentials or setup: {{detail}}. Edit the channel, enter the credentials again, then test the connection.
diagnostics.unhealthy.internal: BlinkEngage could not reach its own file storage: {{detail}}. Nothing in your setup needs changing; contact support if it does not clear on its own.
diagnostics.unhealthy.network: The provider could not be reached at all: {{detail}}. That is either an outage on their side or a network problem between us — check again shortly.
diagnostics.unhealthy.provider: The provider's own servers answered with an error: {{detail}}. Nothing in your setup needs changing — check again once their service recovers.
diagnostics.unhealthy.unknown: The last check on this channel failed without saying where the fault lies: {{detail}}. Test the connection to see the current state, and open the connection log for the full entry.
lifecycle.warning.beta: Complete, and still being proven. Safe to try.
lifecycle.warning.deprecated: This will be removed in a future release. Existing channels keep working.
lifecycle.warning.generic: Worth knowing before you connect this one.
lifecycle.warning.preview: Still under active development. Expect rough edges.
meta.certification.mediaSendFailed: The image uploaded but Meta refused to send it.
meta.certification.noMediaId: Meta accepted the image but did not confirm it was stored.
meta.certification.noMessageId: Meta accepted the message but did not confirm it was sent.
meta.certification.skipped.noTarget: Not tested: no test recipient was given.
meta.certification.subscribeFailed: Meta refused to set up message delivery.
meta.certification.unexpectedError: Not tested: something unexpected went wrong.
meta.certification.webhook.subscribed: Meta is set to send this account's messages to Blink Engage.
meta.check.instagramMessageAccess: Check that message access is on in the Instagram app. Open Settings → Messages and story replies → Connected tools, and turn on “Allow access to messages”. Instagram does not let us check this for you, and messages will not arrive until it is on.
meta.check.noGrant: We have no way to reach Meta as you. Sign in again, or paste an access token.
meta.diagnostic.authentication.expired: The access token has expired. Reconnect the channel.
meta.diagnostic.authentication.expiring: The access token expires in {{days}} days. Reconnect the channel before then to avoid an interruption.
meta.diagnostic.authentication.invalid: Meta says the stored token is no longer valid. Reconnect the channel.
meta.diagnostic.authentication.longLived: The access token does not expire.
meta.diagnostic.authentication.missing: No access token is stored for this channel.
meta.diagnostic.authentication.notAnswer: Meta did not answer. This is usually a short outage or rate limiting on their side — nothing to change here.
meta.diagnostic.authentication.rejected: Meta rejected the stored access token. Reconnect the channel to get a new one.
meta.diagnostic.authentication.unreadabl: Meta reported an expiry date we could not read, so we cannot say how long this token has left.
meta.diagnostic.authentication.valid: The access token works and expires in {{days}} days.
meta.diagnostic.permissions.missing: Meta has not granted: {{scopes}}. Reconnect and approve them.
meta.diagnostic.providerUnreachable: We could not reach Meta. Try again shortly.
meta.diagnostic.webhook.fieldsMissing: Meta is sending us some of this account's activity but not messages. Use Reconnect message delivery to fix it.
meta.diagnostic.webhook.notSubscribed: Meta is not sending us this account's messages. Use Reconnect message delivery to fix it.
meta.diagnostic.webhook.otherAppSubscrib: Another app is also receiving this account's messages: {{apps}}.
meta.error.noResource: Enter the id of the account you want to connect.
meta.error.unreadableResponse: Meta sent a reply we could not read. Try again shortly.
meta.repair.credentialsIncomplete: This channel is missing the account id or access token needed to reconnect. Connect it again.
meta.repair.subscribeFailed: Meta refused to restore message delivery. For WhatsApp and Instagram this is expected — delivery is set on the parent business account, which this action cannot reach. Reconnect the channel instead.
picker.couldNotLoad: We could not load the list of channels. Try again shortly.
picker.needsNewerPlatform: Needs a newer version of Blink Engage. Ask your administrator to upgrade.
picker.noLongerAvailable: No longer available. Existing channels keep working.
picker.subtitle: Choose where your customers message you.
picker.title: Connect a channel
wizard.couldNotConnect: We could not finish connecting. Nothing has been saved.
wizard.couldNotContinue: We could not continue. Check the details above and try again.
wizard.couldNotStart: We could not start setting this up. Try again shortly.
wizard.form.nothingToEnter: Nothing to enter — this channel needs no credentials. Continue to finish.
wizard.oauth.explanation: You will be taken to the provider to sign in and approve access, then brought back here.
wizard.oauth.willAskFor: You will be asked to approve:
wizard.picker.chooseSeveral: You can choose more than one.
wizard.picker.nothingFound: We did not find anything to connect on this account.
wizard.summary.aboutToConnect_one: One channel is ready to connect.
wizard.summary.nameHelp: What your team will see in the inbox. You can change it later.
wizard.title: Connect a channel
